BiblicalUsage: Emesh means yesterday, or last night — the very recent past. The LORD tells Jehu He saw yesterday the blood of Naboth in 2 Kings 9:26, and Laban warns Jacob about what God spoke to him yesternight in Genesis 31:29. It also stretches a little: Job's outcasts flee into the wilderness 'in former time' in Job 30:3, a yesterday that has already gone desolate.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'yesterday' in Scripture is never far away — God remembers what happened last night as clearly as we remember this morning, and His justice does not forget with time. What was done yesterday still stands before Him today, and that is both a warning and a comfort.
